english: Let $A=\begin{pmatrix}3&-1&0\\-1&1&-1\\0&-1&2\end{pmatrix}$. Then the sum of all the entries of $A^{-1}$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $A=\begin{pmatrix}3&-1&0\\-1&1&-1\\0&-1&2\end{pmatrix}$ है। तब $A^{-1}$ की सभी प्रविष्टियों का योग ______ है।
solution_full: The left block is now $I$, so $A^{-1}=\begin{pmatrix}1&2&1\\2&6&3\\1&3&2\end{pmatrix}$.
Check: row $1$ of $A$ times the columns of $A^{-1}$ gives $(3-2,\,6-6,\,3-3)=(1,0,0)$; similarly for the other rows.
originality_note: New: a symmetric tridiagonal matrix with determinant 1 is chosen so that the inverse has integer entries and Gauss-Jordan stays exact (way 5, single routine concept). Closest known: the textbook exercises 'find A^{-1} by elementary row operations' (e.g. NCERT [[1,2,3],[0,1,4],[5,6,0]]). Different because: the matrix and the asked quantity are new; the method itself is standard, as the row of the blueprint intends.

concept_use.Finding inverse by elementary operations: A^{-1} is obtained by reducing [A | I] to [I | A^{-1}] with row operations, and its entries are then added.

stem_review: Read as a student: every matrix and symbol is defined before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed with sympy and is unique and equal to the Answer Plan; no hyperbolic functions or asymptotes. Checked: sympy gives det A = 1, A^{-1} = [[1,2,1],[2,6,3],[1,3,2]] and the sum 21 (a positive 2-digit integer as planned). Changed: No change.
key_step: Carrying out Gauss-Jordan elimination on [A | I] without an arithmetic slip.
justification: Single standard procedure applied over several steps with exact arithmetic and no options; more than the one-move invertibility check of 2026-P1-Q3 (L1), so a routine chain at L2.
